chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali Al-Washā`, from Aḥmad ibn ‘Ā`idh, from Abī Salamah Sālim ibn Mukram, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

When Fāťimah (peace be upon her) became pregnant with Ḥusain (peace be upon him), Jabra`īl (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) and said, “Verily Fāťimah will give birth to a son who will be killed by your nation after you.” Therefore, Fāťimah (peace be upon her) was averse to her pregnancy while she was carrying Ḥusain (peace be upon him), and she was averse to giving birth to him when she did.
Then Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: “Have you ever seen a mother in this world being averse to giving birth to a son?! Her aversion came from knowing that he would be killed.”
He said: And about him (Ḥusain) was revealed this verse,
“We have enjoined on man to do good to his parents; his mother bears him with aversion, and with aversion she gives birth to him; and bearing him and weaning him takes thirty months.”

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: Husain ibn Ali, the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Gabriel, the archangel who delivered the news
key_terms.كَرِهَتْ: She disliked/feared, referring to the specific aversion due to foreknowledge of martyrdom

ai.seo_question: Why was Fāťimah averse to her pregnancy with Ḥusain according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records that Fatimah’s (a.s.) specific aversion to carrying and birthing Husayn (a.s.) stemmed from her prophetic knowledge of his impending martyrdom, distinguishing it from general physical discomfort. This narrative provides a unique exegetical lens for Surah Al-Ahqaf (46:15), where the term 'kurhan' (aversion) is interpreted not merely as physical burden but as the emotional weight of foreseeing the beloved son's death. This highlights the Ahl al-Bayt’s unique spiritual insight into the destiny of the Imams, connecting the verse’s description of parental duty to the specific tragedy of Karbala.
